entities.name: PMID:25435904
observations: Prospective study of 94 biopsy-proven prostate cancer patients undergoing 50-second dynamic perfusion CT.
Prostate cancer was visible as focal peripheral enhancement in 90/94 patients (95.7% detection; reported as 90/94).
Mean perfusion parameters were higher in tumor than normal prostate tissue (p<0.000).
Blood flow and blood volume increased with tumor grade; high-grade tumors had significantly higher blood flow and blood volume.
Authors concluded quantitative perfusion CT can distinguish prostate cancer from normal tissue and may characterize aggressiveness.

entities.name: Prostate cancer
observations: The target study evaluated perfusion CT for detection and grade-related characterization of biopsy-proven prostate cancer.

entities.name: PCT 90 of 94 detection
observations: In a selected cohort with biopsy-proven prostate cancer, perfusion CT visualized cancer in 90 of 94 patients, corresponding to 95.7% apparent detection.

entities.name: PCT grade association
observations: Higher blood flow and blood volume on perfusion CT were associated with higher Gleason grade; this supports biologic characterization but is not independent diagnostic validation.
